program: Local environmental organizing, food justice and youth leadership

what: LVEJO organizes Little Village residents around pollution, land use, food access and environmental justice.
Current campaigns seek stronger industrial review and remediation of contaminated places.
Its farm and community garden also distribute food and provide places for residents to grow culturally meaningful produce.
strengths: Resident organizing addresses pollution and land-use decisions close to affected households.
Active growing spaces provide a concrete food-resource mechanism beyond policy advocacy.
Current campaign descriptions distinguish proposed protections from completed historical wins.
reservations: Proposed ordinances and pending remediation petitions do not establish additional exposure reductions.
Local clinical benefits, net food resources and the response to another gift are judgment-led.
Coalition overlap, industrial relocation, worker losses and housing costs could offset benefits.

sections.what: LVEJO, EIN 36-4259477, is the direct general-support recipient for organizing, food justice, youth leadership and administration. Its Little Village service sites and campaigns lie in Cook County, within the Chicago metro. Headquarters alone is not the geographic evidence: the farm, garden and Collateral Channel work provide local anchors. [Current organization](https://lvejo.org/)
sections.monitoring: Current campaign descriptions identify a proposed cumulative-impact zoning ordinance and a Collateral Channel remediation petition whose status is pending. These are mechanisms and implementation questions, not observed pollution reductions. The food page reports weekly deliveries to over 50 families, garden plots for over 60 families and 2025 production, but not deduplicated annual household use or net resource value. Request implementation dates, exposed population, measured air or water changes, unique households, food substitution and actual participant burdens. [Campaigns](https://lvejo.org/our-work/campaigns/) [Food justice](https://lvejo.org/our-work/food-justice/)
sections.qualitative:
Historical coal closures, cleanup and park conversion demonstrate organizing experience, but are already in the baseline and are not credited again each year or to a new gift. Current prospective protections could improve clinical health only if they actually change exposure beyond existing rules and other coalition work. The model uses separate judgments for implementation probability, LVEJO's coalition contribution and annual funding response. Pollution relocation, unsafe redevelopment, worker losses and displacement remain possible.

The 1,000 local policy-household reference is hypothetical, not a reported cohort. It produces 12.5 expected attributable clinical trajectories after .1 implementation, .25 coalition share and .5 annual response. A .001 annual clinical utility gain for three years after a two-year delay is a finite judgment, not an observed local QALY effect. No permanent coal-closure benefit, citywide mortality reduction or survivor earnings is assumed. Food health effects are not separately stacked on the same cash-equivalent benefit.
sections.cost:
Original 2024 recognized expense is $4,269,375; comparable 2023 and 2022 expenses are $4,090,659 and $3,195,698. Their descriptive mean is $3,851,910.67. The reviewed originals did not identify separate event, rental, gaming or inventory expense groups requiring a revenue addback. This is the whole recipient's recognized accounting boundary; unrecognized volunteer, partner and external compliance resources remain unknown. [2024 original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202543189349305014/IRS990)

Conditional clinical health is 0.0343278 QALYs from 12.5 expected trajectories, three finite years and a two-year delay. Food exposure uses 50 delivery families plus 60 garden families minus 30 judged overlapping households: 80 units. Annual response .5 leaves 40 incremental household units. A judged one-time $300 net resource benefit is halved for health overlap, then the full $50 participant labor/work/travel burden is subtracted in the same household before log. At $20,000 annual household resources and one welfareperson per household, .5 × 40 × log(1 + 100/20,000) / 1.03 = 0.0968455 healthy-year welfare equivalents. Combined 0.1311733 implies $325.476 million per ten combined equivalents. No gross salary or pounds of food is directly treated as QALYs.

Only positive gains receive the overlap adjustment; losses remain full. Clinical-null retains food resources and costs, while zero funding response removes incremental effects. Central policy and payer burden fields are unknown-neutral references, not observed zeros. Worker, rent, compliance and matched producer losses are explicit signed stresses. The joint food-policy case nets same-year household changes before log, or separates different-year household time slices. The headline is a conditional partial-world comparison, not a complete portfolio return or a verified next-dollar donation price.
sections.funding: The 2024 original reports government grants of $196,034. Existing grant support, coalition partners, food distribution and public rules remain in the counterfactual. Ordinary support funds the full LVEJO recipient, not a ring-fenced new ordinance or another historical closure. A priced unfunded staffing or campaign tranche, donor replacement risk and real partner costs were not verified. The official homepage links the 2026 general-support route; its giving-page extractor was unavailable in this review. [Official giving lead](https://lvejo.networkforgood.com/projects/287421-lvejo-2026-general-support)

sources.title: Current food justice projects and reported participation

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized expense; prospective local policy-health and food-resource component. External resources and marginal gift conversion unknown.
model.geographicAttribution: Little Village direct local branch inside Chicago–Naperville–Elgin; statewide or displaced pollution benefits are not assigned automatically.
model.formula: Policy=N*implementation*credit*b; clinical=g*Policy*q*sum finite discount(delay+y) minus full distinct-household harms. Food=(delivery+garden−min(delivery,garden)*overlap)*b. Resources=.5*people*finite discounted log(1+joint signed net/baseline). Combined=clinical+resources; price10=10*C/known positive combined.
model.counterfactual: Historical closures and cleanup, existing rules, food aid, markets, already-funded farms and other coalition efforts continue. No wholesale new-gift credit for completed victories.
model.attribution: Separate enactment/exposure probability, coalition share and annual-package response. Direct food households deduplicated by judgment; one clinical person and one welfareperson per household reference, no family or lifetime multiplier.
model.uncertainty: Observed recipient cost and approximate food scale; clinical conversion, net food dollars and causal funding response are judgments. Full portfolio and outside incidence unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Conditional reference: 12.5 policy clinical trajectories and 40 incremental food household units. These are judged expectations, not measured protected population or causal food outcomes.

inputs.name: C
inputs.rationale: Original 2024 Part IX expense $4,269,375. No separately netted event/rental/gaming/inventory cost group identified in reviewed original; recognized accounting, not complete external social cost.

inputs.name: N
inputs.unit: hypothetical local policy-exposed households, one clinical person each
inputs.rationale: 1,000 is a finite prospective Little Village exposure hypothesis, not observed protected households or entire city population.

inputs.name: implementation
inputs.rationale: Judged .1 additional implemented exposure improvement against existing rules and other advocates. Pending ordinance or petition is not an implemented reduction.

inputs.name: credit
inputs.rationale: Judged .25 coalition causal contribution, distinct from enactment probability and funding response; shared wins not credited whole to every organization.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Judged .5 response of the full annual package relative to continuing grants, farms, government and coalition work; whole recipient cost retained, marginal donor offer unknown.

inputs.name: q
inputs.unit: net annual clinical utility per additionally protected person
inputs.rationale: Judged .001 net clinical utility per year for three years, about .365 healthy day yearly. No local exposure-to-QALY measurement identified; no historical closure replay.

inputs.name: T
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: delay
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: discount
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: delivery
inputs.rationale: Official food page reports weekly deliveries to more than50 families;50 used as approximate conservative scale, not exact dated unique annual household count.

inputs.name: garden
inputs.rationale: Official page reports more than60 garden families;60 used as approximate scale, not a net causal food benefit.

inputs.name: foodOverlap
inputs.unit: fraction of smaller food cohort already in larger cohort
inputs.rationale: Judged .6 of smaller cohort overlaps:50+60−30=80 household units before annual-response adjustment. Measured deduplication absent.

inputs.name: gain
inputs.unit: USD one-time net food/resource benefit before health overlap
inputs.rationale: Judged $300 one-time net food/resource benefit after replacement food aid, taxes, benefits and substitution; no observed dollar outcome or gross job salary.

inputs.name: cost
inputs.unit: USD participant time/work/travel burden per incremental food household
inputs.rationale: Full $50 judged participant labor, work, travel and burden on all incremental food households, retained with failed clinical outcomes.

inputs.name: baseline
inputs.unit: USD annual household resources, one welfareperson reference
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: positiveOverlap
inputs.unit: retained positive resource fraction after health overlap
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: policyBurden
inputs.rationale: Unknown-neutral central0; not observed absence of worker loss, rent burden, compliance, displacement or producer costs. Full signed burdens priced in stress.

inputs.name: policyBaseline
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: foodPolicyOverlap
inputs.unit: policy households also in food cohort, fraction capped by cohort
inputs.rationale: Central disjoint planning hypothesis, not observed independence. Joint sensitivity nets same-year resources before log; different years use explicit household time slices.

inputs.name: payerShare
inputs.unit: matched producer/payer net transfer loss share
inputs.rationale: Unknown-neutral central0, not observed absence of food producer/public payer opportunity losses. Matched signed transfer stress is distinct local household population.

inputs.name: payerPeople
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: payerBaseline
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: harm
inputs.unit: QALY clinical harm per distinct exposed household
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: Chicago MSA share of modeled Little Village branch
inputs.rationale: Finite conditional judgment, not a measured local causal effect; tested in independent scenarios.
